newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers approve Italian EMU plan - EU source.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers approve Italian EMU plan - EU source.

text.p: European Union finance ministers on Monday gave their seal of approval to Italy's plans for meeting the requirements for economic and monetary union (EMU), EU sources said.
They added that a number of ministers had said Italy may need to make more efforts on public finances to make sure it qualifies.
One source said German Finance Minister Theo Waigel had said: "Perhaps other measures will be needed to make a lasting and durable budget consolidation."

French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn was quoted as saying that EU countries needed to take account of the difficult circumstances under which Italy had made budgetary reforms, but other efforts would have to be made.
A statement of conclusions was being drafted for formal approval later.

The Italian blueprint foresees a budget deficit of 3.0 percent of Gross Domestic Product this year, in line with the criterion for EMU. It projects that the ratio will drop to 2.8 percent in 1998. In terms of growth, GDP is expected to rise 1.2 percent this year and 2.0 percent in 1998. - Brussels newroom: +32 2 287-6830
